Implement `paginate(items, page, pageSize)` in `pagination.mjs` as a named export.

Return `{ items, totalPages, nextPage }`, where `items` is a new array of the selected elements in original order, `totalPages` is `Math.ceil(items.length / pageSize)`, and `nextPage` is the next 1-based page number only if it exists, otherwise `null`. Empty input has zero pages and returns empty page data with `nextPage: null`. A page beyond the last returns empty page data with `nextPage: null` while preserving the actual total page count. Do not mutate the input array or its elements.

Implement `dispatch(path)` in `entry.mjs` as the application entry point: it takes an absolute URL pathname string (no query string) and returns `{ route, params }`, throwing `TypeError` for invalid paths (non-string, empty, or not starting with `/`). Matching must be case sensitive and must not alter the pathname text, so a trailing slash is distinct from the route without it. The route ID is a string and `params` is a new plain object. The default routes in `fixtures/routes.mjs` are the production route table used by `dispatch`. Also implement the lower-level exported resolver `resolveFromRegistry(path, records)`, which applies the same matching policy to supplied records.

Supplied `records` are guaranteed to be an array of valid records; invalid record shapes are out of scope. Route IDs and static paths are strings. Dynamic parameter names are unique within each pattern, nonempty, and match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*`; matching paths remain plain pathname strings. Records have one of three shapes: `{ kind: 'static', path, route }`, `{ kind: 'dynamic', pattern, route }`, or `{ kind: 'fallback', route }`. Static paths match exactly. A dynamic pattern starts with `/` and uses `:name` for a whole, nonempty path segment; it may contain literal segments. On a match, return parameters with the original segment values. Among matching records, any static route wins over any dynamic route regardless of declaration order; otherwise the first matching dynamic route wins; fallback is considered only if neither matched. Within static matches, use the first declared static record; if multiple fallbacks exist, use the first declared fallback. With no match and no fallback, return `null`. All records and returned values must remain independent of later calls; do not mutate records. The fixture deliberately lists a dynamic `/users/:id` before the static `/users/new` and includes a fallback to expose ordering.

Repair the CSV order parser and report pipeline, keeping `parseOrders(text)` exported from `parser.mjs` and `buildReport(text)` exported from `report.mjs`.

Input is UTF-8 text with zero or more data rows and no header. Each nonblank row has exactly three comma-separated fields: `SKU,quantity,unitPriceCents`. Accept LF and CRLF line endings and ignore blank or whitespace-only rows. Trim whitespace around each field. SKU must match `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9-]*$`; quantity must be a positive safe integer written in base-10 digits; unitPriceCents must be a nonnegative safe integer written in base-10 digits. Reject non-string text with `TypeError` and any malformed row with `Error`. Reject a row or aggregate whose quantity or cents total exceeds `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with `RangeError`. `parseOrders` returns a new array of `{ sku, quantity, unitPriceCents }` in input order, including repeated SKUs as distinct rows.

`buildReport` must call the parser and return `{ items, totalUnits, totalCents }`. `items` is a new array sorted lexicographically by SKU; each item is `{ sku, quantity, totalCents }` summing all rows with that SKU. `totalUnits` sums quantities across all rows and `totalCents` sums quantity times unitPriceCents. Empty input returns `{ items: [], totalUnits: 0, totalCents: 0 }`. Do not retain state across calls or modify input. Only edit the two listed source files.
